key_insight: Replace the static one-to-one link between vision encoder output and LLM input with dynamic many-to-many cross-layer injections so LLMs can access hierarchical visual features (local to global) on demand.
problem_solved: Overcomes the visual feature bottleneck in current VLMs where a single coarse visual vector limits LLMs' ability to align and reason with multi-scale visual information.
method: Introduce dynamic cross-layer injection modules that connect multiple vision-encoder layers to multiple LLM layers, enabling many-to-many information flow.
Use learned routing/gating (or attention-based selection) to inject relevant multi-level visual features into appropriate LLM layers at inference time.
Keep injectors lightweight and plugin-friendly so the mechanism can be integrated into existing VLMs with modest compute and training overhead.
impact: Enables richer, hierarchical vision–language alignment improving fine-grained understanding and coherent multimodal reasoning; practical for practitioners wanting stronger VLM performance without redesigning full pipelines.

paper_title: From One-to-One to Many-to-Many: Dynamic Cross-Layer Injection for Deep Vision-Language Fusion
paper_authors: Cheng Chen, Yuyu Guo, Pengpeng Zeng, Jingkuan Song, Peng Di
